verdict_reason: 12 tiles found. 11 of them are one photographer's (9751325@N02) single shopping day in the Hanoi Old Quarter, and the pixels put them on at least three different streets: 4434571858 is a hand-carved-stamp shop whose vertical sign reads '6 / STAMP / TAMPON' (the stamp-carvers' trade is on Hang Quat, where the well-known shop is at no. 6), 4433811405 and 4434586026 are a bamboo yard with propped bamboo ladders, tall bamboo poles and hanging bamboo tobacco pipes (the bamboo guild street, Hang Vai), and 4434575630 / 4433793039 are a candied-fruit (o mai) shop with handwritten price jars and a 'BANH CHA - LA CHANH' label (the confectionery street, Hang Duong). Add a packaged-coffee stall on an unrelated street with a clinic at no. 98 opposite, a traditional-instrument-and-lacquer-drum shop, a fried-spring-roll pavement stall and a Christmas toy display, plus one unrelated photographer's cocktail glass. These are separate shopfronts several hundred metres apart pinned to one identical point - the classic effect of one person tagging a whole day's walk at one favourite spot, not a real single location. Note the whole pile is only 3 photographers and 11 of 12 photos are one of them.

photos.evidence: Shot through a shop's glass case at heaped candied and preserved fruit: a plate of dried kiwi and sugared slices, a cone of shredded dried meat/fruit, a bowl of orange preserved kumquat, and dark tamarind-paste blocks stacked in a tower. This is a Hanoi o mai / mut display; the confectionery trade street is Hang Duong. Street name itself not visible.
Rows of identical red plastic roly-poly dolls with painted faces and white Santa-hat trim, stacked on glass shelves in a toy display. No signage, no architecture, no street.

Black-and-white close-up of a receding row of glass jars of coffee beans stencilled 'COFFEE MO-N...', with others reading 'DA...' and 'SP...' behind. A coffee retailer's shelf; no shop name, number or street.

Pavement scene: a woman and a suited man sitting on plastic stools beside stacked cartons of G7 and 'Nescafe Cafe Viet' coffee. Across the narrow street, three-storey shophouses with concertina steel gates, a wrought-iron balcony, and a clinic banner reading '...SIEU AM MAU ... XET NGHIEM ... GIAM DOC: BAC SI TRAN THI ... GIO LAM VIEC 8h00 DEN 17h00 HANG NGAY', with a red vertical sign bearing the house number 98 beside it. Winter clothing and leaf-off trees. The name and street on the banner are blown out and unreadable at this resolution, so only the Old Quarter shophouse fabric is usable.

A pavement stacked two storeys high with dozens of finished bamboo ladders and bundles of long bamboo poles, chained together, leaning against the shopfront; motorbikes and leaf-off street trees behind. Bamboo ladders and poles sold in bulk on the pavement is the bamboo guild street, Hang Vai.

Wall of a packaged-coffee stall: glass jars stencilled 'WEASEL' numbered 1-7, jars labelled 'COFFEE SPECIAL', 'HIGHLAND', 'COFFEE DARKEN', 'MOKA', boxes of Nescafe Cafe Viet and stacks of G7 sachets. The street behind shows Old Quarter shophouses with an orange awning and an illegible dark shop sign. Same stall as 4433803351; no street name legible.

Woman in an orange top sitting on a blue plastic stool at a pavement cooking pitch, frying spring rolls; sooted steel splash-back, stacked enamel bowls, plastic buckets, tiled wall. Entirely interior-to-the-stall; nothing identifies the street.

Narrow shop crammed with traditional Vietnamese instruments hanging on the back wall (dan nguyet, dan ty ba, dan nhi, moon-shaped lutes) plus stacked red-and-gold lacquered ceremonial drums, hand drums and black lacquer boxes; a mirror at the back shows two customers. A Hanoi Old Quarter instrument/lacquer shop, but no sign or number readable.

A stamp-carver sitting on a stool cutting a wooden stamp at a low bench outside his shop, racks of finished carved wooden stamps and carved wall plaques on display, and a white vertical shopfront sign reading '6' at the top over 'STAMP' and 'TAMPON'. Next door is an old dark-timber shophouse with an iron lattice front and a carved wooden hanging sign (illegible). Hand-carved-stamp shops are the trade of Hang Quat, where the best-known one is at no. 6, matching the '6' on the sign.

Two tiers of tall glass jars of dark preserved fruit (o mai) with handwritten price cards - '8.000', '7.000', '1.000' with 'MO GUNG', 'MAN CHUA', 'MAN XAO GUNG' style labels - over a glass counter holding bagged sweets and labels reading 'BANH CHA - LA CHANH ... 10.000 dong', 'HUONG CAT - CO TRUYEN 10.000 dong' and 'BOT SAN DAY NGUYEN CHAT'. Banh cha and o mai sold this way is the Hang Duong confectionery street; no street plate in frame.

Two women on plastic stools in front of a shopfront filled with dozens of standing bamboo canes and leafy bamboo stems, brooms at the left, and at the right a rack of dark bamboo tobacco pipes and thin bamboo rods hanging against a peeling stucco wall. Bamboo poles plus bamboo smoking pipes is specifically the Hang Vai bamboo trade.
Close-up of a cocktail in a martini glass with lime wedges, on a woven placemat with cutlery. No window, sign or view; nothing locational.
